newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: KOF company survey sees no Swiss upturn in Q1.
newsitem.headline: KOF company survey sees no Swiss upturn in Q1.

text.p: The Swiss economy shows no signs of rebounding from its weakness in the first quarter of 1997, according to a survey by the Swiss Institute for Business Cycle Research (KOF) at the Federal Institute of Technology (ETH).

"Results of the KOF/ETH survey of 6,000 companies show the economic situation has clearly deteriorated. No improvement is expected for the first quarter," it said in a statement. The sector surveys were conducted in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"Thus the KOF/ETH prognosis published in January 1997 that the economy would stagnate in 1997 is further confirmed by the latest surveys," it said.
It said industry cut more jobs as order inflow and production remained stagnant. Constructions firms continued to see bleak conditions and expected prices to fall.
Retails sales are likely to drop again in the first quarter as unsatisfactory business conditions prevail.

"In the hotel and catering sector, the weakening of the Swiss franc and the early onset of winter created a positive influence, especially for the tourism sector. But in all turnover remained below year-earlier levels," it said.
